name: Prove It!

pick.label: Pick an activity
pick.heading: Pick something and put a check on it
lead: These days you prove your age to buy wine, to see some films and, in more and more countries, to open a social media account. Every check keeps somebody out, annoys somebody else and gets dodged by a fourteen-year-old with a VPN.
Choose an everyday activity that nobody has ever thought needed a check, and design one. Here are some ideas, but you can choose your own. *The more pointless, the better.*
pick.hint: Or click one to choose it.
pick.note: Obviously nobody is going to turn this into law. It’s just for a bit of fun, and to get us thinking about who a check keeps out, who it lets through, and who it annoys on the way.

shelf.head: At home
items: Choosing the film on a Friday
Adding someone to the family group chat

rows: Which activity are you putting a check on?
Who is it meant to stop, and who else gets caught by accident?
A test, a document, a face scan, a password, a quiz, a bouncer with a clipboard…
How people will get round it:
Be honest: how long before someone finds a loophole, and what is it?
Time, money, privacy, the patience of honest people…
How would you persuade people that your check is a good idea?

values.who: Anyone who can’t say what they want in under a minute. Mainly my friends and, I’m sorry to say, me.
values.how: The Voice Note Licence. Before your message goes, a little box asks you to sum it up in one sentence. If you can, it’s sent as a text instead. If you can’t, you have to wait ten minutes and think about what you’ve done.
values.dodge: Typing “see voice note” into the box. My students found this in about four seconds.
values.cost: Ten minutes of everyone’s day, and the end of my mother’s eight-minute updates about the neighbours’ cat, which I would secretly miss.
values.sell: Less talking, more saying. Or, for the German market: “Kurz und gut.”

yours.label: Your check
yours.heading: Your idea
yours.lead: Fill it in on your own phone or laptop (it stays on your device), and be ready to tell the class about your check in a few sentences.

rank.label: The ranking
rank.heading: Which check wins?
rank.placeholder: The check, e.g. The Voice Note Licence
rank.lead: Each student tells us about their check in a few sentences. Add it, then argue it into place: the one most likely to work at the top, the one a fourteen-year-old would dodge fastest at the bottom.
